body.statement: The envelopes satisfy \(\mathcal C_P=\{u\in C(X_0):\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L,\ \ell_P\le u\le r_P\}\), and \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\) if and only if \(\ell_P(x)\le r_P(x)\) for every \(x\in X_0\).
body.justification: The result converts latent-model compatibility into an observable necessary-and-sufficient envelope test.
body.gap: Existing conditional-moment methods provide general tests, but no exact obstacle certificate for these coupled baseline-specific cones.
body.consumer: Researchers can distinguish rejection of the maintained bounded-trend model from mere failure of point identification.
body.proof_tex:
By the declared support types, \(H\) is a nonempty compact subset of \(I\times(I-I)\), and the first coordinate \(d\) of every \((d,z)\in H\) belongs to \(X_0\).  Indeed, if \((d,z)\in\operatorname{supp}_P(X,Z)\), every product neighborhood of \((d,z)\) has positive \(P\)-probability, so every neighborhood of \(d\) has positive \(P_X\)-probability and hence \(d\in\operatorname{supp}_P(X)=X_0\).

By \(\mathrm{ass:continuous\mbox{-}regression}\), \(g\) is continuous on \(H\).  It is bounded there: for each \(q\in H\), continuity supplies a relative neighborhood \(U_q\) on which \(|g|<|g(q)|+1\); compactness supplies a finite subcover, and the maximum of the corresponding finitely many bounds is a finite uniform bound.  Thus both suprema and infima in \(\mathrm{def:obstacle\mbox{-}envelopes}\) are finite.

For every \((d,z)\in H\), define, only within this proof,
\[
a_{d,z}(x)=g(d,z)-K|z|-L|x-d|,
\qquad
c_{d,z}(x)=g(d,z)+K|z|+L|x-d|.
\]
The reverse triangle inequality gives, for \(x,x'\in X_0\),
\[
|a_{d,z}(x)-a_{d,z}(x')|
 =L\bigl||x-d|-|x'-d|\bigr|
 \le L|x-x'|,
\]
and the same inequality holds with \(a_{d,z}\) replaced by \(c_{d,z}\).  If a family \(\{f_j\}\) is pointwise finite and every \(f_j\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz, then
\[
\sup_j f_j(x)-\sup_j f_j(x')
 \le \sup_j\{f_j(x)-f_j(x')\}
 \le L|x-x'|;
\]
interchanging \(x\) and \(x'\) proves that its pointwise supremum is \(L\)-Lipschitz.  Applying this argument to \(-f_j\) proves the corresponding fact for a pointwise infimum.  The maximum or minimum of an \(L\)-Lipschitz function and a constant is also \(L\)-Lipschitz, because the maps \(v\mapsto\max\{c,v\}\) and \(v\mapsto\min\{c,v\}\) are one-Lipschitz.  Therefore \(\ell_P\) and \(r_P\), as defined in \(\mathrm{def:obstacle\mbox{-}envelopes}\), are finite-valued, \(L\)-Lipschitz, and hence continuous on \(X_0\).

We next prove the equality of classes.  Let \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  The Lipschitz and support-cone clauses in \(\mathrm{def:feasible\mbox{-}trend\mbox{-}class}\) imply, for every \(x\in X_0\) and \((d,z)\in H\),
\[
u(x)\ge u(d)-L|x-d|
       \ge g(d,z)-K|z|-L|x-d|=a_{d,z}(x).
\]
The level clause of the same definition gives \(u(x)\ge-M\).  Taking the supremum over \((d,z)\in H\) and then the maximum with \(-M\), exactly as in \(\mathrm{def:obstacle\mbox{-}envelopes}\), yields
\[
u(x)\ge \ell_P(x).
\]
Similarly, the same two clauses give
\[
u(x)\le u(d)+L|x-d|
       \le g(d,z)+K|z|+L|x-d|=c_{d,z}(x),
\]
and the level clause gives \(u(x)\le M\).  Taking the infimum and then the minimum yields
\[
u(x)\le r_P(x).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathcal C_P
\subseteq
\{u\in C(X_0):\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L,
                   \ \ell_P\le u\le r_P\}.
\]

For the reverse inclusion, let \(u\in C(X_0)\) satisfy \(\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L\) and \(\ell_P\le u\le r_P\).  The outer maximum and minimum in \(\mathrm{def:obstacle\mbox{-}envelopes}\) give
\[
\ell_P(x)\ge-M,
\qquad
r_P(x)\le M,
\]
so \(-M\le u(x)\le M\) for all \(x\in X_0\), and therefore \(\|u\|_\infty\le M\).  For an arbitrary \((d,z)\in H\), evaluation of the supremum and infimum at that same support point gives
\[
\ell_P(d)
 \ge g(d,z)-K|z|-L|d-d|
 =g(d,z)-K|z|
\]
and
\[
r_P(d)
 \le g(d,z)+K|z|+L|d-d|
 =g(d,z)+K|z|.
\]
Since \(\ell_P(d)\le u(d)\le r_P(d)\), these inequalities imply
\[
|g(d,z)-u(d)|\le K|z|.
\]
Thus all three membership clauses in \(\mathrm{def:feasible\mbox{-}trend\mbox{-}class}\) hold, so \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  This proves
\[
\mathcal C_P
=\{u\in C(X_0):\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L,
                  \ \ell_P\le u\le r_P\}.
\]

If \(\mathcal C_P\ne\varnothing\), choose \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  The established characterization gives \(\ell_P\le u\le r_P\), hence \(\ell_P(x)\le r_P(x)\) for every \(x\in X_0\).  Conversely, suppose \(\ell_P(x)\le r_P(x)\) for every \(x\in X_0\).  Take \(u=\ell_P\).  The first part of the proof shows that \(u\in C(X_0)\) and \(\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L\), while the assumed inequality gives \(\ell_P\le u\le r_P\).  The characterization therefore gives \(u\in\mathcal C_P\), proving \(\mathcal C_P\ne\varnothing\).
